title: Owner discovery farm
description: Child processes that discover the admission facts of owners in parallel, because the discovery of one owner is single-threaded JavaScript that takes 4 to 65 s cold and the admission closure observed hundreds of them one after the other. The children are the walk children of the closure farm (one JSON line per request and answer, a child that dies, stalls or ends on memory is replaced, a failure only makes the parent discover the owner itself) running `./👷️deriver`; they are booked as `walk-farm` workers of the one memory plan of the process tree, so they never exceed the share the project farm leaves. A child holds a whole owner (hundreds of thousands of observed rows), so it is booked at childBytes and recycled at recycleBytes. The parent never waits for a child: an owner is discovered by the parent itself unless a child is ready.

format.description: The admission format of the parent: a child whose own format differs refuses, so no child discovers with another implementation than the parent holds.

epoch.description: The caches of one attempt (the native manifests and closures) live for one epoch: a child drops them when the epoch changes, as the parent creates them again for every attempt.
